answer: Each metre of firn core is weighed as it comes out of the drill, and the density log files the weight beside the depth for the whole core. A bridge metre claimed as weighed fails the log: the core must have been pulled from the firn at the thread of the drilling, and a metre never weighed has no density to file. Forging a core means bribing the driller, faking fifty weighings and paying 13,100, and the yarrow log is read against the ice-core store, so a metre whose weighing was never entered crumbles as a claim.
